q: 1. A member with a cross section of a mm² is subjected to a force of P N. It is L mm long and of Young's Modulus, E N/mm². The strain will be
explain: Strain = stress/E = (P/A)/E = P/AE, a dimensionless ratio (mm/mm).

q: 2. Find the elongation of a bar if c/s area of bar is A, length l, applied load p, modulus of elasticity of material is E
explain: Standard elongation formula: δ = PL/AE.

q: 3. If α is the coefficient of linear expansion, T is the rise in temperature then thermal stress is given by
explain: Thermal stress (fully restrained) = E·α·T.

q: 4. Thrust is induced in case of
explain: Thrust (axial force along the member) develops from the component of an inclined load along the member's axis.

q: 5. The diagram showing the variation of axial load along the span is called
explain: Axial load variation along a member's length is plotted as a thrust diagram.

q: 6. Dead load of a member is the
options: one that occurs due to dead body
one that comes all of a sudden
one that comes due to self weight of the object
explain: Dead load is the permanent self-weight of the structure/member itself.

q: 7. Stress in a beam due to simple bending, is
explain: Bending stress varies linearly (directly proportional) with distance from the neutral axis, σ = My/I.

q: 8. The maximum shear stress will always occur at
options: a fibre in the cross-section depending on configuration
explain: For a rectangular section max shear stress is at the neutral axis, but for other shapes (I, T, etc.) the maximum location depends on the section's geometry.

q: 9. In the case of H section the maximum shear stress will occur at
options: at the junction of web and flanges
explain: In H/I sections, shear stress peaks at the web-flange junction due to the sudden width change.

q: 10. If all the dimensions of a bar are increased in the proportion n:1, the maximum stress produced in the prismatic bar by its own weight will increase in the ratio
explain: Self-weight stress scales linearly with the linear dimension scale factor n, giving a ratio of n:1.

q: 11. If magnitude and direction of a load does not change with respect to time, this type of load is called
explain: A load constant in magnitude and direction over time is a static load.

q: 12. The number of reaction components at a hinged end of a general loading is
explain: A hinge (pin) support provides two reaction components (horizontal and vertical) but no moment.

q: 13. If the elasticity of the material is zero then the material is said to be
explain: Zero elasticity means the material shows no elastic recovery — it deforms plastically.

q: 14. An orthotropic material has
options: different properties in three perpendicular directions
explain: Orthotropic materials have distinct material properties along three mutually perpendicular axes (e.g. wood).

q: 15. If a material has identical properties in all directions, it is said to be
explain: Isotropic means direction-independent material properties.

q: 16. An isotropic material has
explain: Isotropy is typically associated with homogeneous material composition throughout.

q: 17. A visco elastic material
explain: Viscoelastic materials exhibit both viscous and elastic behavior, meaning their stress-strain response depends on time/rate.

q: 18. A brittle material has
explain: Brittle materials fracture with minimal plastic deformation, i.e. a very little plastic zone.

q: 19. The compression test is commonly used for testing
explain: Brittle materials (like cast iron, concrete) are typically much stronger in compression, so compression tests are standard for them.

q: 20. A brittle material will
explain: Brittle materials fracture suddenly with little to no prior warning (no significant plastic deformation).

q: 21. The brittle materials have low toughness because they
options: undergo large plastic deformation before failure
undergo small plastic deformation before failure
undergo no plastic deformation before failure
explain: Low toughness in brittle materials results from very limited plastic deformation absorbing energy before fracture.

q: 22. A body having similar properties throughout its volume is said to be
explain: Homogeneity means identical properties at every point/volume of the body.

q: 23. The moment of inertia of an area will be least with respect to
explain: By the parallel axis theorem, moment of inertia about the centroidal (central) axis is always the minimum for any set of parallel axes.

q: 24. The square root of ratio of moment of inertia and cross section area of a member is known as
explain: Radius of gyration k = √(I/A) by definition.

q: 25. The radius of gyration of a rectangular section is not proportional to
options: square root of the moment of inertia
square root of the inverse of the area
square root of the moment of inertia divided by area of the section
explain: k = √(I/A) — it depends jointly on I and A together, not on 1/A alone.

q: 26. The moment of inertia of a square section is given by
explain: For a square of side b, I = b⁴/12 (special case of bd³/12 with b=d).

q: 27. The moment of inertia of a rectangular (B×D) section about its base is
explain: About the base (not centroid), using parallel axis theorem: I_base = BD³/12 + BD(D/2)² = BD³/3.

q: 28. The moment of inertia of triangular section b×h about the base is
explain: Standard formula: I_base = bh³/12 for a triangle of base b and height h.

q: 29. The moment of inertia of triangular section b×h about the c.g. is
explain: Standard formula: I_cg = bh³/36 for a triangular section.

q: 30. Centre of gravity of a semi circle is ___ above the base AB (diameter)
explain: Standard result: centroid of a semicircular area lies at 4r/3π from the diameter.

q: 31. The c.g. of a semi-circular arc is
explain: As per the answer key for this set.

q: 32. Centrifugal force acts at a curve
explain: Centrifugal force is the outward pseudo-force acting away from the center of curvature.

q: 33. Centrifugal force is given by
explain: Centrifugal acceleration/specific force = v²/R (per unit mass form used in this option set).

q: 34. Centrifugal force acts away from the center of the path while centripetal force
options: acts away from the center of path
acts towards the centre of path
explain: As per the answer key for this set.

q: 35. A cable subjected to U.D.L. over its entire span assumes a shape of
explain: A cable under uniformly distributed load (per horizontal length) hangs in a parabolic shape.

q: 36. The algebraic sum of the shear flow of a section in any direction must be equal to
explain: Shear flow forms a self-balancing internal system, summing to zero around a closed section.

q: 37. The shear center may be defined as
options: the point through which the resultant of the shear stress passes
the point about which the moment of shear flow of section is zero
the shear force in that direction
explain: The shear center is the point of application of transverse load through which no twisting occurs — the resultant shear stress passes through it.

q: 38. The shear center in the case of a T-beam section is
options: at the C.G. of the section
at the neutral axis of the section
on the C.G. horizontal plane and away from C.G. within the leg projections
explain: For a T-section, the shear center coincides with the centroid due to its axis of symmetry.

q: 39. The maximum number of transverse shear forces possible at one end of an element of a plane frame are
explain: At each joint of a plane frame element, up to two transverse shear components can exist (in-plane, general loading).

q: 40. The maximum number of transverse shear forces possible at one end of an element of a plane truss are
explain: Truss members carry only axial force (two-force members) — no transverse shear develops at the ends.

q: 41. The law "Stress is proportional to strain within certain limits" is formulated by
explain: Hooke's Law states stress ∝ strain within the elastic limit.

q: 42. According to Hooke's law which one is correct?
explain: Hooke's Law: stress = Modulus of Elasticity × strain, i.e. σ = Eε.

q: 43. The zone between elastic limit and proportional limit on the elastic curve of an elastic material is known as
explain: Beyond the proportional limit but still within the elastic limit, stress-strain is no longer linear — this is the non-linear elastic zone.

q: 44. As per elastic theory of design the factor of safety is the ratio of
options: ultimate load to load at yield
explain: Factor of safety (elastic design) = yield stress / working (permissible) stress.

q: 45. Which of the following gives Poisson's ratio?
options: ratio of linear stress to linear strain
ratio of shear stress to shear strain
ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain
explain: Poisson's ratio μ = lateral strain / longitudinal strain.

q: 46. The value of Poisson's ratio always remains
explain: For all real engineering materials, Poisson's ratio lies between 0 and 0.5, always less than one.

q: 47. Normally the numerical value of Poisson's ratio is
explain: Typical values: steel ≈ 0.3, concrete ≈ 0.15.

q: 48. The phenomenon of decreased resistance of material due to reversal of stress is called
explain: Repeated/reversed stress cycles progressively weaken a material — this is fatigue.

q: 49. The property of a material by which a body returns to its original shape after removal of the force, is called
explain: Elasticity is the ability to recover original shape/size after unloading.

q: 50. A perfectly elastic body is
options: that body which recovers its original shape completely after removal of force
a body of such a material with a lot of extensibility
a body made of rubber only
a body whose cross sectional dimensions are very small
explain: By definition, perfect elasticity means complete shape recovery on unloading, regardless of material or size.
